q: A warehouse trainee tells a driver, calmly and with a nod toward the loading board, that his pallets will be ready at Door 6 in ten minutes. She is:
o: demonstrating verbal and non-verbal communication consistently in a clear, concise and effective manner

q: Which statement would best help a driver find the right loading door?
o: "Your load is at Door 6, to the left of the office."

q: A trainee studies a chart of late deliveries by day, notices Mondays are worst and explains the pattern to her supervisor with the numbers. She is:
o: reading numbers aloud with no meaning
analyzing, interpreting and effectively communicating information, data and observations

q: A good report of late-delivery data should include:
o: what the numbers show and what they likely mean

q: A trainee notices a forklift driver waving his hand and pointing at a blocked aisle and moves the pallet right away. She is:
o: observing and interpreting verbal and nonverbal cues to enhance communication

q: A coworker says he is fine but keeps rubbing his sore wrist and avoiding the lift. A good teammate would:
o: ask if he needs help or a break

q: A trainee takes notes on a dispatcher's route changes and repeats the new times back to confirm them. She is:
o: applying active listening skills to obtain and clarify information

q: Repeating instructions back to the speaker is useful because it:
o: confirms the message was understood correctly

q: A trainee sees that scanner errors keep slowing the dock, so she tests the battery, then the Wi-Fi signal, then the label quality and discusses the findings with her team. She is:
o: employing critical-thinking skills independently and in groups to solve problems and make decisions

q: When a team solves a problem together, critical thinking helps by:
A trainee sees the packing station jam every afternoon and maps each step to find where boxes pile up before suggesting a new layout. She is:
o: analyzing elements of a problem to develop creative and innovative solutions

q: Mapping each step in a process helps a worker:
A trainee correctly uses terms like 'pallet jack', 'bill of lading' and 'SKU' while following a supervisor's directions. She is:
o: demonstrating the use of content, technical concepts and vocabulary when analyzing information and following directions

q: Why is it important to know the exact meaning of a term on a shipping form?
o: A wrong meaning can send the wrong goods to the wrong place

q: A trainee wears her safety shoes, follows the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) rules posted on the dock and checks that aisles are clear before moving a load. She is:
o: understanding and consistently following workplace safety rules and regulations

q: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) sets standards to:
o: protect workers from hazards on the job

q: A trainee sees a worker slip on spilled oil, stays with him, alerts her supervisor and helps complete the incident report. She is:
o: demonstrating knowledge of procedures for reporting and handling accidents and safety incidents

q: After an accident on the dock, the first priority is to:
o: get help for anyone who is hurt and keep the area safe

q: A trainee scans every package on her cart, keeps the area neat and asks for more work when her tasks are done. She is:
o: demonstrating a positive, productive work ethic by performing assigned tasks as directed

q: What does a productive work ethic look like during a slow hour?
o: Finding useful tasks without waiting to be told

q: A trainee finds a box with the wrong label and weighs whether to quietly ship it or report it, deciding to report it. She is:
o: applying ethical reasoning to make an ethical decision

q: Which choice is the most ethical response to a mislabeled package?
o: Report it so it can be corrected

q: A trainee follows the legal limits on how much weight a cart may carry and logs her inspection each shift. She is:
o: complying with all applicable rules, laws and regulations in a consistent manner

q: Following load-weight regulations is important because they:
o: help prevent equipment failure and injuries

q: A trainee in a supervised placement at a distribution center completes a pick-and-pack task, writes down what she did and reviews it with her mentor. She is:
o: conducting, documenting and evaluating learning activities in a supervised distribution and logistics experience

q: Why should a trainee document her learning activities?
o: So she can review progress and identify what to improve

q: A trainee learns to read inventory software reports under her mentor's guidance to reach the level needed for her chosen job. She is:
o: developing advanced technical knowledge and skills related to her occupational objective

q: Advanced skills for a logistics job are best developed through:
o: guided, hands-on practice in a real setting

q: A trainee's records show her order accuracy rose from 90 percent to 98 percent over a semester. She is:
o: demonstrating growth of technical skill competencies

q: Which record best shows skill growth?
o: A log with accuracy scores from the start and end of the term

q: A trainee compares her checklist to the job requirements and sees she is strong at scanning but weak at route planning. She is:
o: evaluating strengths and weaknesses in technical skill proficiency

q: Identifying a weakness is useful when it leads to:
A trainee saves a completed shipment log, a photo of a labeled pallet and her supervisor's note in a folder. She is:
A student is picking items for her logistics portfolio. Which choice is the most representative of her real work?
o: A filled-out inventory sheet she completed herself
A blank template from the internet
A page she made up for show
e: Samples must be her own typical work.
